g.text: 1. Clinker (lap-strake) planking, 13 strakes of 15 mm mahogany, landed on 12 grown oak frames.

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: 2. Strakes overlap the plank below by 22 mm, fastened with clenched copper roves - the clinch work

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: described by Falconer (1769) and visible in RMG SLR1818.

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: 3. Five thwarts, double-banked (10 oars); stern sheets abaft the after thwart.

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: 4. Floor gratings on cleats; two large keelson eyes fore and aft for the davit slings.

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: 5. No rudder or rowlocks are shown on the RMG model (SLR1818); oars and a steering sweep are

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: carried as loose gear, as was usual for a boat stowed on davits.
